Path 3, AWSGOALS §10.3

Karpenter, KEDA and VPA

Nodes, signals and pod size: three layers, three tools.

WHAT IT IS

Karpenter provisions right-sized nodes fast. KEDA scales workloads on external signals like Kafka lag or Prometheus queries. VPA, now with in-place pod resize, adjusts requests without restarts.

WHAT SETS IT APART

KEDA reacts to the signal we actually care about, not CPU. In-place resize changes the HPA and VPA calculus. Letting all three act on one workload is how autoscalers fight.

WHERE WE STAND

Trial KEDA on one Kafka consumer: KEDA for the signal, VPA for the size, Karpenter (or Auto Mode) for nodes.

"Autoscaling at Scale with KEDA" (Stripe); "In-Place Pod Resizing Like I'm 5" (AWS), KubeCon NA 2026
